# `silk/platform/native/process`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Runs a child process with the system calls, for the native `ChildProcess` provider.

## When to use
`silk.system.child_process_native` uses [`NativeProcess.execute`](#NativeProcess.impl.execute). Application code uses the `ChildProcess`
effect from `silk.system.child_process` instead.

## Details
Each call owns its descriptors, its copies of the request, and its child. If a step fails after
the child started, the call stops and waits for the child, closes the descriptors, and then
returns the first error.

## Gotchas
- The calls block the thread.
- A trap does not clean up, and does not stop the child.

Import as `NativeProcess` with `import silk.platform.native.process { NativeProcess }`.

<a id="NativeProcess.impl.execute"></a>

### Associated function `execute`

```silk
pub effect fn execute(request: &ProcessRequest) -> ProcessOutcome
    ! ProcessError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Starts the program of `request`, waits for it to end, and returns its outcome with all of
its output.

#### Details
The child gets the arguments and the environment of the request, and the working directory
of the request, or of the parent when it is empty. Its standard input is closed. A failure
to start is an error. An exit code that is not 0, and an end by a signal, are outcomes.

#### Gotchas
The call blocks the thread. Do not wait for the child in other code. If a step fails after
the child started, the call stops and waits for the child, closes the descriptors, and then
returns the first error. A trap does not clean up, and does not stop the child.
